newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices rise on welcome CPI numbers.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices rise on welcome CPI numbers.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Wednesday, aided by slightly lower than forecast April inflation data and a general rise in European bond prices after Tuesday's Federal Reserve meeting left U.S. interest rates unchanged.
Dealers said that the 10-year yield gap to the German bund narrowed as a result of the 1.7 percent rise in the CPI, compared to a forecast 1.8 percent.
"It created some interest at the long end of the market, flattening out the yield curve somewhat," a trader said.
At 1130 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.52 point from Tuesday's close, at 111.44.
The forthcoming benchmark seven percent state bond due 2007 rose 0.58 point, to 104.00, yielding 6.45 percent.
The yield gap between the 2006 bond and the German bund narrowed to 49 basis points from its earlier 51 bp and the 2007-bund gap shrank to 68 basis points from 69.
The crown firmed to 3.8077 per mark, from Tuesday's 3.8082. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
